newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India up again, Taiwan strong.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India up again, Taiwan strong.

text.p: Indian GDRs extended recent gains on Thursday as buying interest continued in steady trade, dealers said.

They said the market saw good two-way business in key stocks after the local market registered large volumes earlier. A dealer said the recent strong run could slow ahead of the February 28 budget, but major declines over the period were not expected.
He said good two-way business was seen in BSES, Indian Hotels, Hindalco, Gujarat Ambuja and SBI.
Hindalco collected 43 cents to $26.50/$27.50 and SBI made 35 cents to $19.37/$20.37.
A trader said interest in second-tier stocks was limited, and expected the Indian market to trade in a tight range ahead of the budget.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) benchmark 30-share index rose 9.17 points, or 0.26 percent, to 3,492.65.
The Indian GDR index JCEAI closed at 70.89, up 0.52 points or 0.74 percent with the premium over the local market at 17.99 percent from 17.39 percent on Wednesday.
Taiwanese GDRs made strong gains following a run in U.S. technology stocks overnight and a rise to six-year highs for Taiwan stocks.
The Taiwan GDR Index closed at 106.31, up 2.65 points or 2.56 percent, a premium of 5.20 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended at 66.91 points, up 0.56 points or 0.84 percent and the premium at 43.90 percent over the local market.
Korean stocks were driven up by higher prices for DRAM chips, and hopes for a further recovery in the prices. Samsung made 76 cents to $21.75/$22.75.
